retroposon insertions can generate new functional human genes.
retroposon insertions into the POTE gene have generated new functional POTE genes.
the human genome contains a new functional gene that arose from an ancestral POTE gene by retroposon-mediated insertion of a functional actin gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genes that may play an important role in human cancer.
the identification and characterization of the POTE gene, a primate-specific family of 13 related genes.
the evolution and expression of POTE–actins, which are expressed in a limited number and variety of normal tissues but in a wide variety of cancer cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
POTE is a primate-specific protein that has evolved by duplication, remodeling and retroposon-mediated insertion of an actin gene into the POTE–ANKRD26 ancestral gene.
POTE is a new human actin gene that evolved by insertion of a retoposon into an ancestral POTE gene and is expressed in a limited number and variety of normal organs and many different cancer cells.
the human genome is a mosaic of old, new, functional and nonfunctional genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

POTE genes have evolved from an ancestral gene by duplication, retroposition, and remodeling of the genome, and that POTE gene family proteins are expressed in many cancers and in a limited number in normal organs.
the POTE gene is expressed in a limited number and type of normal organs, but in a broad spectrum of cancers, and that the POTE protein is involved in cancer progression.
the POTE genes evolved from the ANKRD26 gene by a series of duplications and remodeling events.
